description.value: First Nations-owned oceanfront and woodland resort near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, with ocean-view and woodland tent sites, flush washrooms, and a playground; tap water is non-potable so bring your own drinking water.

address.value: #1 Cluxewe Campground Road, PO Box 245, Port McNeil, BC V0N 2R0

raw_osm.description: Campsite and picnic area. Water available, but not potable due to manganese issues (2022). Registration at RV resort office. Pebble beach. Alternate kayak landing in estuary.
raw_osm.name: Cluxewe Resort Campsite

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content fetched from cluxeweresort.com (tent-camping page, FAQ, contact, and RV-sites subpages) provides extensive primary evidence. The OSM tag drinking_water=no is corroborated verbatim by multiple website passages confirming non-potable tap water. Showers, laundry, ice, and online reservations are explicitly listed on the RV-sites and tent-camping pages. Contact details (phone, address) appear on the /contact/ subpage but are absent from OSM tags, so they are sourced from the website and flagged.
concerns: OSM record has no address or phone number; both sourced from website /contact/ page (#1 Cluxewe Campground Road, PO Box 245, Port McNeil, BC V0N 2R0; 1-250-949-0378) — contact_confirmed fields cannot be verified against OSM.
Tap water is explicitly non-potable — touring cyclists must carry sufficient drinking water for the entire stay; this is a critical practical concern for this listing.

OSM description attributes non-potable water to 'manganese issues (2022)'; website (copyright 2026) confirms the issue persists, adds iron as a co-factor, and notes a 2026 upgrade is in progress — the OSM description should be updated to reflect current status.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active First Nations–owned campground with tent sites on a cycling-relevant corridor through northern Vancouver Island; good amenity coverage, online booking, and a strategic location for North Island touring routes. Clear fit for the WWC directory.
enrichment_extras.notes: WiFi and cell service available on-site per FAQ, though service may be limited due to remote location. Camp store sells sundries and souvenirs. Bear activity noted in resort policies — guests explicitly warned not to leave food waste or garbage in campsites.

wow_evidence: First Nations-owned oceanfront and woodland resort
